page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n2-standard-2 in the lower performance tiers for most compute-intensive and memory-bound operations. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, while multi-core performance falls into the poor category. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only small block cached speeds of 102.01 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds of 13.8 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10 percent. However, single-threaded gzip compression demonstrates average performance in the middle 50 percent tier at 23.81 GB/sec. Other tests, such as Geekbench software compiling, ray tracing, and image processing, consistently register in the bottom 10 percent, alongside static web serving throughput of 1.95 GB/sec and small-model LLM inference speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-2 offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level workloads that do not require high-performance compute or massive memory arrays. Given its dedicated CPU allocation and standard memory density, it is suitable for basic general-purpose tasks, lightweight background utilities, small-scale development environments, and low-traffic web serving. The lack of local storage and lower benchmark scores for database operations and multi-core processing make it less suitable for heavy database hosting, large-scale data compilation, or real-time rendering.
